st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb on all sides for about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and cook 4 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, turmeric, cinnamon, pepper, and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots and turnips and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini and chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes more, until the lamb and vegetables are tender.
While the stew finishes, put the couscous in a large heatproof bowl with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and rub it between your fingers.
Pour [[2.5 cups]] boiling water over the couscous, cover tightly, and let it stand for 10 minutes.
Add the [[2 tbsp]] butter and fluff with a fork, breaking up any clumps.
Mound the couscous on a big platter and top with the meat and vegetables. Serve the broth in a bowl alongside.

ing: or large flour tortillas, torn in small pieces
st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb for 8 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, paprika, cumin, harissa, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, and the pepper.
Add the grated tomatoes, whole chili, and [[5 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the chickpeas and simmer 10 minutes more, until the lamb is very tender.
Toast the flatbread pieces in a 300°F (150°C) oven for 10 minutes until dry and crisp-edged.
Put the torn bread in a large serving dish and ladle over enough hot sauce to soak it, keeping a little for the table.
Toss gently until the bread softens but is not mushy, about 2 minutes.
Top with the lamb and chickpeas and serve at once with the extra sauce.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the lamb with the onion for 8 minutes until browned.
Stir in the tomato paste, cinnamon, pepper, and [[2 tsp]] salt for 1 minute.
Add the grated tomatoes and [[7 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and the freekeh. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the wheat is soft and the lamb is tender.
Add half of the cilantro and the mint and cook 5 minutes.
Taste for salt. If the soup is too thick, add a little hot water.
Ladle into bowls, scatter with the remaining cilantro and mint, and serve with lemon wedges.

ing: plus 1 cup cold for the flour
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and cook the lamb and onion over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, and pepper for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, half of the cilantro, and [[6 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Add the lentils and chickpeas and simmer for 25 minutes more until the lentils are soft.
Whisk [[2 tbsp]] flour into [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until completely smooth with no lumps.
Slowly pour the flour mixture into the soup while stirring and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thick.
Add [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the rest of the cilantro. Cook 5 minutes, then taste and adjust.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and bread or dates.

ing: rechta, or angel hair or fresh thin pasta
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and cook the onion and garlic over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken, cinnamon stick, turmeric, pepper, and [[2 tsp]] salt and stir for 3 minutes.
Pour in [[6 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the turnips and chickpeas and simmer for 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the turnips are tender.
The sauce should be thin and pale. If it is too watery, simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Boil the noodles in a large pot of salted water for 3 to 4 minutes, or following the package, until tender, then drain.
Toss the hot noodles with [[2 tbsp]] butter and a ladle of the broth.
Pile the noodles on a platter, top with the chicken, turnips, and chickpeas, and pour over more broth. Serve hot.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Brush a 9x13-inch baking dish generously with olive oil.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] chickpea flour with [[2.5 cups]] water until completely smooth with no lumps.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes so the flour can hydrate.
Whisk in the eggs, [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, cumin, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the pepper.
Pour the batter into the dish.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set in the middle, firm to the touch, and golden on top.
Cool for 10 minutes so it firms up, then cut into squares.
Serve warm, tucked into bread with harissa if you like.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and bell peppers for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, chili, cumin, and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the pepper. Simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and jammy.
Make 6 small wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5 to 8 minutes, until the whites are completely set. The yolks can stay soft if you like, or cook longer for firm.
Scatter with the cilantro and bring the pan to the table. Serve with crusty bread.
Mix the semolina, flour, and [[1 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Add the warm water slowly, kneading for 8 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, coat with some of the oil, cover, and rest 30 minutes.
For the filling, heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onions and bell pepper for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, paprika, cumin, and [[1 tsp]] salt, then the tomatoes. Simmer 15 minutes until thick and dry. Cool.
On an oiled surface, stretch or roll one ball very thin into a square about 8 inches wide.
Spread [[2 tbsp]] of filling over the middle and fold the edges in toward the center to make a square packet.
Heat a dry or lightly oiled skillet over medium heat. Cook each packet for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Repeat with the remaining dough. Serve hot.
Mix the semolina, flour, yeast, sugar, and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add the egg, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, and about [[1 cup]] warm water. Stir and then knead for 10 minutes into a soft, smooth dough, adding a splash of water if it feels dry.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise in a warm spot for 1 hour, until puffy.
Divide into 2 balls and press each into a disc about 1/2 inch thick on a floured surface.
Prick the tops with a fork and let them rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook one disc for 8 to 10 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through, with a hollow sound when tapped.
Repeat with the second disc. Cool slightly on a rack and serve warm with butter or soup.

ing: melted, plus 1 tbsp for the dates
st: Mix the semolina with a pinch of salt and pour in the melted butter. Rub it with your hands for a few minutes until every grain is coated.
Add [[1 tbsp]] orange blossom water and about [[0.5 cup]] water a little at a time, kneading to a smooth dough. Rest for 30 minutes.
Mash the dates with [[1 tbsp]] butter, the cinnamon, and [[1 tbsp]] orange blossom water into a thick paste. Roll into thin logs.
Roll the dough into long ropes the thickness of your thumb. Press a groove down the center of each.
Lay a date log in the groove and pinch the dough closed around it, then roll gently to seal.
Flatten the filled ropes slightly and cut them diagonally into diamonds about 2 inches long.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the pieces in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden. Drain.
Warm the honey with [[0.25 cup]] water and the last [[1 tbsp]] orange blossom water in a pan for 3 minutes.
Soak the warm pastries in the warm honey syrup for 2 minutes, then lift out and cool on a rack.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the ground almonds, [[1.25 cups]] powdered sugar, [[3 tbsp]] flour, and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Add the egg, [[2 tbsp]] melted butter, [[2 tbsp]] orange blossom water, and the almond extract if using.
Knead into a smooth, firm paste. If sticky, add a spoonful of ground almonds. If dry, add a few drops of water.
Roll the paste into 24 balls about the size of a walnut.
Press your thumb into the center of each ball and pinch the sides up to make a small cup, then set on the baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until pale golden at the edges. They will be soft and firm up as they cool.
Cool on the pan for 10 minutes, then dust with the remaining [[0.25 cup]] powdered sugar.
Rinse and dry the chicken. Rub with the ginger, turmeric, garlic, salt and pepper and leave 15 minutes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken 4 minutes per side until golden, then set aside.
Add the grated onions to the pot with a pinch of salt. Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until they melt into a soft jammy base.
Return the chicken, add the saffron with its water, [[1.5 cup]] broth and half the cilantro. Cover and braise on low for 35 minutes.
Blanch the olives in boiling water for 2 minutes to remove excess brine, then drain. Add them with the lemon to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the chicken reads 175°F and the sauce is thick and glossy.
Scatter with the remaining cilantro and serve with crusty bread or couscous.
nt: Seared, then braised in a covered pot
Best swap: for a one-pan oven version bake covered at 350°F for 45 minutes. Use green olives plus extra lemon zest if you lack preserved lemon.
